experts.name: Aswath Damodaran
experts.quote: the most telegraphed 3rd quarter number of all time
experts.summary: On the amendment's Q3 numbers. He values Anthropic at about $1.48 trillion and says he will sit out if it prices well above that; he won't short it.

experts.name: Dan Ives
experts.quote: you could call it 1.5, is maybe baseline ... to what probably could even go lower by mid-November.
experts.summary: Still bullish on Anthropic's importance, but sees $1.5T as the baseline for valuation talk and calls an expected junk credit rating a 'gut punch'. Quoted secondhand.

experts.name: Dylan Patel
experts.quote: Anthropic could even be the first company to be a $10 trillion valuation company in the world.
experts.summary: He says Anthropic's inference economics already cover compute costs, and it could reach roughly $1T of revenue around 2028-29, which would support a $10T valuation. Elsewhere he has argued OpenAI and Anthropic will control most usable compute by 2028.

experts.name: Ed Zitron
experts.affiliation: EZPR (CEO); Where's Your Ed At newsletter; Better Offline podcast
experts.quote: Anthropic's leaked IPO prospectus showed that it spent $2.75 to make a dollar in 2025, making it a worse business than OpenAI.
experts.summary: Using 2025 figures ($12.6B spent, $7.33B of it on compute, for $4.6B of revenue and an $8B operating loss), he calls Anthropic a structurally unprofitable 'dog'. He mocks bulls who say 2025 doesn't count.

experts.name: Gary Marcus
experts.affiliation: NYU professor emeritus; Marcus on AI (Substack)
experts.quote: Anthropic ARR is flatlining post tokenmaxxing (as many of us predicted) just as they are about to IPO.
experts.summary: He says growth has stalled and profits rest on 'adjusted' figures. Frontier models are commoditizing against cheap open-source rivals, so a $2T market cap doesn't add up, and retail investors and pension funds could be left holding the bag.

experts.name: Gil Luria
experts.quote: Anthropic will end up being a very speculative investment. They may do well, they may not.
experts.summary: He says Anthropic peaked in enterprise earlier in 2026, then slowed as OpenAI caught up and customers moved to cheaper open-weight models. He prefers the hyperscalers and chipmakers that get paid either way, and calls the labs' safety-slowdown rhetoric a bid to consolidate power.
experts.outlet: CNBC interview via Business Insider (syndicated on AOL)

experts.name: Jay Ritter
experts.affiliation: University of Florida, Warrington College of Business ('Mr. IPO')
experts.quote: a lot of things have to go right
experts.summary: Only 14 of 4,110 US IPOs from 1980 to 2024 priced above 40 times sales, and they trailed the market by 15.4% on average. A value above $1.4T needs a path to $100B or more of annual after-tax profit.

experts.name: Mark D. Levine
experts.affiliation: New York City Comptroller (trustee/adviser to NYC pension funds, >$325B)
experts.quote: I write to urge Anthropic to pause its planned initial public offering (IPO) until the company fully and transparently addresses the artificial intelligence (AI) safety, governance, and development pace concerns it has raised.
experts.summary: Because Anthropic itself warns of catastrophic or existential AI risk and has called for slowing capabilities, he argues it should pause the IPO. He wants it to set out audits, controls and timelines, and says concentrated founder/trustee control widens the gap between control and accountability.
experts.outlet: Office of the NYC Comptroller (letter PDF)

experts.name: Matt Levine
experts.summary: A frontier-AI prospectus forces the company to choose what good vision of AI to promise and what bad vision to warn about. Next to SpaceX's huge market-size claim and OpenAI's AGI pitch, he calls Anthropic's framing relatively restrained. The same issue also covers share classes.

experts.name: Michael Burry
experts.quote: For the benefit of humanity, the markets should tank hard and prevent the OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs.
experts.summary: Burry, who holds puts on AI-linked stocks, argues the labs will destroy trillions of dollars of capital. He says a market sell-off that blocks their IPOs would be the lesser harm.

experts.name: Tomasz Tunguz
experts.quote: Building a business that went from $41M to a $16B half-year in three years is without precedent.
experts.summary: Bull case: 11.9x growth on a derived ~40% gross margin, the first operating profit (~$974M in Q2), positive cash flow and almost no drawn debt. Bear case: $637B of commitments (his sum of the seven named deals in the original S-1), two-thirds non-cancelable, against consumption revenue customers can cut.

experts.name: Zvi Mowshowitz
experts.affiliation: Don't Worry About the Vase (Substack); AI-safety-community commentator
experts.quote: this seems entirely appropriate to me, and I also think it makes the company more valuable rather than less valuable.
experts.summary: He defends founder control plus the LTBT as appropriate and value-enhancing, while understanding investors who won't buy under it. He doubts the LTBT has much real leverage beyond appointing ordinary business people to the board. He called Q3 revenue of $16.8B 'highly disappointing'.

experts.name: Ann Lipton
experts.affiliation: University of Colorado Law School (corporate/securities law)
experts.quote: public shareholders will have very few governance rights.
experts.summary: Without significant changes, public shareholders in Anthropic get almost no governance rights. Founders hold 50.1% of votes through Class F, and the LTBT elects the board majority.
experts.outlet: Wall Street Journal (paywalled), quoted by Business Model Analyst (2026-10-19)

experts.name: Azeem Azhar
experts.quote: It is a business whose revenues are growing far faster than its costs.
experts.summary: Behind the $8B 2025 operating loss and $42B net loss (inflated by an accounting charge), he sees a company investing for growth that shows 'green shoots'. Revenue outpaces costs, but about $410B of the $518B commitments cannot be cancelled.

experts.name: Benedict Evans
experts.summary: Per the recap, OpenAI and Anthropic, each valued near $850-900B privately, were together worth more than every venture-backed company that IPO'd in the 1995-2000 dot-com boom. Either valuations correct, a lab builds a moat nobody has yet invented, or labs capture enough application-layer value to justify the price.
experts.outlet: ben-evans.com presentation, via Advertiser Intelligence recap

experts.name: Brett Winton
experts.quote: the frontier lab companies will be good for the bill
experts.summary: The world is short of compute, and the leading labs can pay for what they have signed.

experts.name: Campbell Hutcheson
experts.quote: very strong growth, high gross margins
experts.summary: Paying up for short-term compute is rational; the fundamentals are still strong while the company invests heavily in research.

experts.name: Chris Hughes
experts.summary: The AI sell-off reflects oil, rates and geopolitics as well as the overhang of the Anthropic listing. Reports of disappointing revenue growth hurt confidence, and getting the deal done would help clear the air.

experts.name: Dave Lee
experts.summary: He reads the S-1's dire warnings about the company and humanity as a deliberate 'anti-sell'. Like a recruiting pitch, it repels poor-fit investors and attracts believers.

experts.name: Harrison Rolfes
experts.quote: you need to bump that gross margin up to like 70%
experts.summary: He estimates gross margin at about 44%, well short of the ~70% at Microsoft or ServiceNow, and thinks Anthropic needs about 70% to carry commitments that run to 2030-32.

experts.name: J. Bradford DeLong
experts.quote: Anthropic should study Netscape and its fate.
experts.summary: He expects the model layer to commoditize like the browser did, leaving thin profits for model sellers. IPO buyers should keep Netscape in mind.

experts.name: Kyle Guske II (New Constructs)
experts.affiliation: New Constructs (senior investment analyst; independent research)
experts.quote: In short, we don't think Anthropic has a viable business.
experts.summary: A reverse-DCF that deducts $518B of commitments finds $2T needs ~56% revenue CAGR through 2035 at a 10% margin. A mature-company case (20% margin, 20% growth) gives about $144B, 93% below $2T. The note calls it 'the most ridiculous IPO of 2026' and mainly exit liquidity for insiders.
experts.outlet: New Constructs report via The Next Web / 24/7 Wall St.

experts.name: Matt Kennedy
experts.quote: I wouldn't say these results are worrisome, but I do expect some of this pressure on growth and margins ... to be reflected in the ultimate IPO valuation
experts.summary: Q3 isn't alarming, but slower growth and thinner margins should lower the IPO price.

experts.name: Reuters Breakingviews (columnists)
experts.summary: The listing would be a public-market audit of what has so far been mostly private enthusiasm for AI. The $2T ambition could slip again to after the November US elections.

experts.name: Tae Kim
experts.quote: Anthropic would be foolish to include a bad October ARR number when it doesn't have to and it's not foolish.
experts.summary: He reads the blank October-ARR placeholder as a sign the number will be good. He highlights 1,900+ $1M customers, revenue growth far ahead of compute spend and positive operating cash flow. He flags TSMC and memory supply as the binding risk.

experts.name: Tony Trzcinka
experts.quote: The key question is whether revenue can compound fast enough to absorb the future commitments and outpace compute cost
experts.summary: A credit investor's view: the $895.4B of commitments against revenue growth is the crux.

experts.name: Anders Bylund
experts.quote: At Anthropic, Wall Street gets to pick up the tab for the compute bills, but it will never get a seat at the table.
experts.summary: Public investors get economic exposure but no real say, because the founder LLC has 50.1% of votes and the LTBT elects the board majority. Buyers should be comfortable with that before investing.

experts.name: Kathleen Hanley
experts.quote: For the most part, one should not expect short-run profits right after trading
experts.summary: Retail buyers shouldn't count on a quick first-day pop in these mega-IPOs.

experts.name: Martin Peers
experts.summary: The IPO roadshow collides with Anthropic researchers publicly putting AI-catastrophe odds above 10%, and with internal reports that raised model-derailment risk from 'very low' to 'low'. That leaves the company with an awkward disclosure tension.

experts.name: Simeon Hyman
experts.quote: [S]afety incidents could adversely affect company performance.
experts.summary: Safety is a financial risk as well as an ethical one. Incidents could bring regulation, compliance costs and product delays.

experts.name: Tim O'Reilly, Ilan Strauss, Isobel Moure
experts.quote: We cannot govern markets we don't understand.
experts.summary: They wanted the S-1 to disclose circular cloud deals with investor-suppliers, cap-table detail, training-data litigation and operating and safety metrics, and argued existing SEC rules already require much of it. Useful as a checklist to score the actual S-1 against.

bull_args.title: Growth with improving unit economics
bull_args.argument: Revenue went from $41M in 2023 to $33.2B in the first nine months of 2026. Q2 was the first quarter with an operating profit ($974M); Q3 slipped to a $567M loss after a $2.0B non-cash donation charge, for a nine-month operating loss of $1.3B. Operating cash flow was +$6.6B over nine months and adjusted operating income $4.1B (S-1/A pp. 138, 172). Revenue is growing faster than costs.

bull_args.title: The scary net loss is mostly an accounting mark
bull_args.argument: $94.3B of the $104.0B nine-month 2026 net loss, and ~$34B of the $42B 2025 loss, are non-cash fair-value charges on convertible notes, SAFEs and derivatives as the company's value rose. Economically, the operating line and cash flow matter more.
attributed_to: Gil Luria (D.A. Davidson, per CNBC snippet)

bull_args.title: Inference already pays; the upside is enormous
bull_args.argument: Revenue minus compute cost is already positive. Enterprise adoption is deep (1,900+ customers paying $1M+ a year), and if revenue approaches ~$1T by 2028-29, Anthropic could be the first $10T company.

bull_args.title: Compute is financeable and the balance sheet is strong
bull_args.argument: Lenders and suppliers (Broadcom, Google) have financed capacity against contracted payments, so financing is not the near-term bottleneck. Anthropic has essentially no drawn debt, a large cash pile and $14.8B available on its revolver.

bull_args.title: Scarcity, index demand and a governance structure that can add value
bull_args.argument: It is the first major gen-AI pure play, Ives calls it 'the heart and lungs of the AI revolution', and Nasdaq-100 fast entry forces index buying. Zvi argues founder control plus the LTBT makes the company more valuable, and Ritter's data show dual-class tech IPOs have historically outperformed.

bear_args.title: The price needs heroic assumptions
bear_args.argument: $1.5-2T needs 30%+ operating margins and sky-high growth (Damodaran) and is ~31x the July run-rate (PitchBook). A mature-company DCF gives ~$144B (New Constructs). The private valuation alone could buy ~78 profitable S&P 500 companies (Burry). Good company is not the same as good investment (Ritter).

bear_args.title: The leverage is hidden in compute commitments
bear_args.argument: $895.4B of compute commitments as filed in the amendment, of which $213.8B is terminable or conditional (pre-amendment estimates ran $518B–$637B) set against consumption revenue with no lock-in. The payments are owed whether customers stay or not. Rolfes thinks ~70% gross margins are needed to carry them, against ~44% now.

bear_args.title: Growth is slowing as models commoditize
bear_args.argument: OpenAI caught up and enterprises shifted to open-weight models (Luria). ARR is 'flatlining' (Marcus) and Q3 was 'highly disappointing' (Zvi). Model-selling may go the way of Netscape (DeLong), and reports of weak revenue growth shook the AI trade (Hughes).

bear_args.title: Revenue quality, concentration and circularity
bear_args.argument: ARR is unstandardized and gameable, and Anthropic books cloud-marketplace revenue gross (Damodaran). Nearly half of 2025 sales ran through Amazon and Google, who are also investors, suppliers and competitors. The top five customers were about 25% of nine-month 2026 revenue, though none exceeded 10%. The 2025 cost base was $2.75 per $1 of revenue (Zitron).

bear_args.title: Public shareholders carry the risk without control, amid existential-risk disclosures
bear_args.argument: Class F gives seven founders 50.1% of votes and the LTBT elects the board majority, so public holders get 'very few governance rights' (Lipton). The NYC Comptroller wants the IPO paused over a 'gap between control and accountability'. The company's own catastrophic-risk warnings are a 'shocker risk' (Ives), and safety incidents are a financial risk (Hyman). Burry and Hendricks argue the AI-risk rhetoric serves the labs themselves.
